idiom_name: match statement with class, sequence, mapping and guard patterns
implementation_notes: Python 3.10 added match/case as syntax: class patterns deconstruct through __match_args__ (dataclasses provide it), sequence, mapping and literal patterns test structure, guards add side conditions and as-patterns bind the whole subject. The interpreter performs no exhaustiveness check - a subject matching no case is a silent no-op - so keep a type checker in the loop: end the match with case _: and call typing.assert_never(...), and mypy's exhaustive-match error code or pyright's reportMatchNotExhaustive can check the statement directly. Use match for values whose shapes are genuinely a closed set, and validate untrusted input first, because a pattern tests structure, not invariants.
pitfalls: Without a final assert_never arm, or exhaustive-match enabled, the match is unchecked and silently does nothing for an unhandled shape.
__match_args__ is positional: reordering the fields of a dataclass silently changes which attribute a positional class pattern binds.
A bare name is a capture pattern, not a comparison - case RED: matches and binds anything; value patterns must use a dotted name such as Color.RED.

variants.name: Typed if/elif chain with assert_never (pre-3.10 runtimes)
variants.idiom_name: isinstance chain closed by typing.assert_never over a Union or Enum
variants.implementation_notes: On 3.8/3.9, or wherever a chain fits better than a match statement, dispatch with if/elif isinstance and close the chain with typing.assert_never (Never from typing_extensions); the type checker then proves the final branch unreachable and fails when a union member or enum member is not handled. That bottom-type call is what supplies the exhaustiveness guarantee match alone does not have, at the cost of the terser pattern syntax - and it composes with ordinary boolean conditions, which match guards cannot. Use this variant while a codebase has not moved to 3.10, or where mypy/pyright exhaustiveness checking is already part of CI.
pitfalls: assert_never raises only if it is reached at run time; the guarantee comes from running the checker in CI, not from the interpreter.
isinstance dispatch cannot express payload patterns (nested structure, literals), so nested cases degrade into manual field tests that the checker does not verify.
